title: On the Closed-Form of Flow Matching: Generalization Does Not Arise from Target Stochasticity

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The underbrace asserts u^{cond}(x_t, z=x_1, t) = (x_1 - x_t)/(1-t) = (x_1 - x_0)/(1-t). With x_t := (1-t)x_0 + tx_1 (defined immediately after in the text), one has x_1 - x_t = (1-t)(x_1 - x_0), so (x_1 - x_t)/(1-t) = x_1 - x_0: the (1-t) cancels and no (1-t) remains in the denominator. The printed final equality would require x_t = x_0, which holds only at t=0. The paper itself confirms the correct target in Algorithm 1 (u^{cond}(x_t,t) = (x_1 - x_t)/(1-t) = x_1 - x_0) and in the Figure 1 caption (u^{cond}((1-t)x_0+tx_1, z=x_1, t) = x_1 - x_0), so the extra (1-t) denominator in Equation (5) is a genuine isolated algebraic error in an annotated simplification.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1, Empirical flow matching (paragraph following Proposition 2)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Proposition 2(ii) (proved in Appendix B.3, Eqs. (40)-(62)) states the exact equality E[\hat{u}^\star_M(x,t)] = \hat{u}^\star(x,t), and Appendix B.1 claims 'This important detail yields an unbiased estimator'. Yet the main text in Section 4.1 states the estimator 'does not guarantee unbiasedness in the standard Monte Carlo sense' and that 'the theoretical claims therefore approximate unbiasedness within empirical tolerance'. This directly contradicts the formal proposition and its proof; the hedging prose is an internal inconsistency that was not reconciled with Proposition 2.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix B.3, proof of Proposition 2(iii), Equations (70)-(73)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Equation (70) gives n·(1/M)·E_{Unif}[\sum_j w^{(i_j)}(u^{(i_j)})^2]. Since the indices are i.i.d. uniform, E_{Unif}[\sum_{j=1}^M w^{(i_j)}(u^{(i_j)})^2] = M·E_{l~Unif}[w^{(l)}(u^{(l)})^2], so the correct value is n·E_{l~Unif}[w^{(l)}(u^{(l)})^2] = \sum_l w^{(l)}(u^{(l)})^2. Equation (71) instead writes only E_{i_1~Unif}[w^{(i_1)}(u^{(i_1)})^2], dropping the factor n, and the same missing n propagates into Equations (72)-(73). The RHS of (73) should read \sum_l w^{(l)}(u^{(l)})^2 - (\hat{u}^\star)^2 = Var[u^{cond}] for the stated comparison to hold. The final inequality (74) is nonetheless true, but the displayed intermediate algebra is inconsistent by a factor n.

Equation (28) carries an explicit 1/n factor in front of the sum; Equation (29) - obtained by evaluating the delta-function integral - drops the 1/n without any stated reason. Taken literally, the ratio of Equation (29) (numerator) over Equation (26) (denominator, which retains its 1/n) yields n·\hat{u}^\star, not \hat{u}^\star. The final closed form (Equation (6)) is correct, so this is a missing-1/n typo in the derivation chain, but the printed proof is internally inconsistent.

Both Table 1 and Table 2 are captioned 'FID FMNIST', while the surrounding text states 'We present below the results for the MNIST dataset'. Moreover the two tables report order-of-magnitude-inconsistent FID values for the same method and epoch (e.g., CFM at epoch 5: 15.30 in Table 1 vs 253.56 in Table 2; CFM at epoch 10: 4.20 vs 48.67), strongly suggesting Table 1 (lower FIDs) refers to MNIST and Table 2 to FMNIST, so at least one caption is mislabeled.

summary: Uncertainty-mode verification (lenient strictness, threshold 0.30) over 74 snippets: 48 high-uncertainty snippets were routed to specialist verifiers (36 to verify-math, 5 to verify-text, 5 to verify-vision, 2 to verify-citation), the remainder accepted as low-risk. Five findings survived aggregation. The most serious is a genuine algebra error in Equation (5): the underbrace simplifies u^{cond}(x_t, z=x_1, t) to (x_1-x_0)/(1-t), but with x_t = (1-t)x_0 + tx_1 the (1-t) cancels and the correct target is x_1 - x_0; Algorithm 1 and the Figure 1 caption in the same paper use the correct form, so the error is isolated to that displayed equation. Secondary issues: (i) Section 4.1 text claims only approximate unbiasedness for an estimator that Proposition 2(ii) proves exactly unbiased - an internal contradiction; (ii) the proof of Proposition 2(iii) drops a factor n in Equations (70)-(73) (the final variance inequality is nonetheless correct); (iii) the proof of Proposition 1 drops a factor 1/n in Equation (29) (the final closed form is nonetheless correct); (iv) Appendix C labels both tables 'FID FMNIST' although the surrounding text concerns MNIST and the two tables' values are inconsistent by an order of magnitude. Core theoretical results (the closed-form velocity field, the unbiasedness and variance-reduction claims of Proposition 2) and the main empirical narrative are otherwise internally consistent. Given the >=0.85-confidence error in a central equation of the loss, the paper requires correction.
